A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same identity-bias and response-anonymization study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix reordering.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM debate experiments, including identity-bias measurements, accuracy comparisons, and analyses of personas, peer counts, and debate rounds.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and additionally reports a qualitative analysis of five Llama3.1-8B failure cases on GPQA.

M1.justification: The identity-weighted DCM framework and response-anonymization procedure are unchanged. Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same removal of self/peer attribution, prompt templates, and randomized response order.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GPQA Diamond, GSM8K, MMLU Professional Medicine, and HellaSwag. The added failure analysis selects cases from the existing Llama3.1-8B/GPQA setting and does not introduce new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions compare vanilla and anonymized MAD with the same model and persona configurations. The new failure analysis uses this existing comparison; no additional competing method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v5 Appendix J adds a diagnostic selection procedure: five Llama3.1-8B GPQA cases correct in both settings in the first round, but correct after debate only under standard MAD. Existing benchmark splits, sample counts, decoding settings, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 Appendix J adds a focused qualitative analysis of cases where anonymization fails to preserve a correct answer. The existing DCM validation, persona, peer-count, debate-round, and Appendix A case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 retains the same pooled maximum-likelihood estimators. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the five-case diagnostic sample does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and all existing plotted results are unchanged. Appendix J newly reports four selected cases reaching incorrect conclusions under anonymization and one producing lengthy reasoning without a final answer.

T1.justification: The definitions, Theorem 1, Corollary 1, IBC decomposition, multi-peer derivations, and martingale proof are unchanged. v3 Appendices J and K.1 correspond to v5 Appendices I and J.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unifying sycophancy and self-bias, modeling identity-weighted belief updates, introducing anonymization and IBC, and improving debate trustworthiness.

C2.justification: A new Appendix H FAQ explicitly recognizes identity cues as potentially useful expertise priors and discusses controlling their influence. Appendix J tentatively interprets the newly reported failures as base-model susceptibility to flawed persuasion or indecisive reasoning. Earlier limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9, the 2048-token limit, L40S/H200 hardware disclosures, and all prompt templates. The code-release statement and repository address are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Choi and Li (2026), Modex: Evaluator-free best-of-n selection for open-ended generation, to the discussion of majority-driven convergence. The expanded main related-work section otherwise reproduces v3 Appendix D, preserving the research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained verbatim. v5 incorporates the extended related-work discussion into Section 6, removes a redundant preliminary summary, reorders supplementary sections, and changes citation style and author-header formatting.

P2.justification: The single-column presentation becomes a two-column main text and early technical appendices, substantially reflowing equations, prompt boxes, tables, and surrounding prose. Existing figures are retained and repositioned; the debate-round and multi-peer plots exchange Figure 4/5 numbering.

improvement.justification: v5 adds failure-focused evidence to the existing accuracy discussion and explicitly acknowledges useful expertise cues, modestly improving transparency and discussion of applicability. The five selected cases do not establish the suggested attribution to base-model limitations, so the gain is limited. The main empirical evidence and theory remain unchanged.
